meta.machine: AMD EPYC 7642 / Ubuntu 24.04.4 / kernel 6.8.0-134 / ext4 / 4 vCPU, 8 GiB.
meta.counts: 77 scenarios / 752 supported cells / 14,264 measured observations + 752 warmups.
meta.verdict: Nift is usable for bounded Nift-owned automation, but large-tree throughput is weak here. At 10k files, its walk is 1.350s, stat 3.055s and mixed workflow 8.553s; Go takes 39.767ms, 73.877ms and 300.728ms. I choose .f for small project-local tasks when its APIs suffice; Python or Go for a new general release utility.
meta.diagnostics: Cloud walk/stat traces show 21,373/41,373 metadata queries at 10k files. Stat allocation profiling records 5,578,191 calls. A minimal read-loop chained call executes three times; explicit binding executes once. Accepted adapters use binding and pass exact checks. Core remains untouched.
